races.name: Racing To School Celebrates 25 Years Lady Amateur Jockeys Handicap Stakes (For Female Amateur Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with multiple placings on Good ground, this step up from 7f to 1m on the straight Ascot mile is the main query given all five recent starts have been at seven furlongs or shorter.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and has sound form at 7f-8f on Good, trainer in form at 1/8 over 14 days; the step to a mile is not a concern and she handles this going, but eight placings from fifteen similar-going runs without winning flags consistency questions.

runners_data.name: Stratocracy
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a solid record at 7f on Good ground but has not broken through at this trip; trainer Kevin & Lauren Frost had a runner in the last 14 days, and the horse's five-run form string shows a level but unremarkable profile at this class.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with headgear (t), recent runs all on Stansted going rather than Good turf which is a clear concern; trainer Gary & Josh Moore are in excellent form at 3/31 over 14 days, and the horse ran only 10 days ago suggesting fitness is sharp.

runners_data.name: Atmosphere
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with visor applied, two of her last five runs have been at 8f on Standard and she handles the step up in trip; 50 days between runs is the notable flag, but she has placed on Good ground before and her late-running style is suited if the pace over-develops.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with visor, has placed consistently at 8f on Good ground across recent starts and the course and distance profile fits well; the 3/8f/GOO run in recent history is encouraging, though she has yet to win at this level.

runners_data.name: Tex
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with headgear (tp), has both won and placed at 7f-8f on Good ground recently and her 30-day absence is not alarming; her best Ascot-type form over 8f on Good (2nd) suggests she could get involved if the front runners tie each other up.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner in the field, she has a string of placed efforts at 8f on Good and soft going; running only 6 days after her last start is worth monitoring, but the lack of any genuine pace rival means she has every chance to control this race from the front.

runners_data.name: Bold Suitor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with solid placed form in this type of contest, though his natural prominent style means he is likely to find the front-rank already occupied by Little Empire and Cancan In The Rain before he can settle into his preferred position — the chance depends on adaptability.

runners_data.name: The Bitter Moose
runners_data.note: Has a strong record of placing at 6f-7f with the visor, but all five history runs show Standard going rather than Good, and as a genuine hold-up type whose true rear position is squeezed in this field, he races with positional compromise that makes his scoring difficult to engineer here.

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern for a hold-up runner in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace; recent form includes several wide-margin defeats and the horse has raced just six days ago — his true hold-up role is further compressed by the field's depth of rear-runners.

races.paceDynamic: Eazy On The Eye is the sole confirmed front runner in this 11-runner mile handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is positioned to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on Good ground at Ascot. Little Empire, Cancan In The Rain, Stratocracy, and Calyxoh are all legitimate prominent types who will push forward behind her, creating a medium-tempo race where the front rank remains relatively compressed through the first half-mile. The hold-up horses — Dannick, Atmosphere, and Tex — will settle in behind this group, but with a controlled pace they face the challenge of generating enough late momentum to close. This field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the pace map can place naturally — Bold Suitor, The Bitter Moose, and Port Louis are true prominent or hold-up runners redistributed to midfield, meaning the immediate chasing pack will be more congested than the map suggests, with Little Empire and Cancan In The Rain most likely to secure their natural front-rank positions. The race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent running style that can travel smoothly behind Eazy On The Eye and pounce when the pace inevitably steadies into the Ascot straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Eazy On The Eye leads at a measured gallop and the prominent runners track her without undue pressure.
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits horses who settle close to the action and produce a sustained finishing effort from two furlongs out rather than a sharp sprint; Ascot's straight mile rewards those who conserve energy through the first half before pressing forward.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Eazy On The Eye is allowed a completely uncontested lead and slows the race to a virtual crawl.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to close the gap early, Eazy On The Eye banks a significant lead through the middle portion and her recent run of placed efforts under similar conditions suggests she can grind out a narrow victory if the pace is pedestrian enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rattle Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong and burns off the prominent horses, leaving the finishers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Atmosphere and Tex have both shown ability to come from off the pace, and if the prominent group overdoes it tracking Eazy On The Eye on good ground, there could be room for late closers to benefit from a strong pace collapse into the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Bold Suitor or other redistributed types push forward aggressively and turn this into a messy scramble.
scenarios.body: A congested mid-race tempo disrupts the prominent runners' rhythm and creates a bunched finish where shorter-priced horses fail to dominate; horses racing out of role are less likely to deliver, and this scenario relies heavily on redistributed types performing outside their natural running position.

watchPoints.text: Eazy On The Eye sets the entire pace architecture here — if Miss Thomasina Eyston elects to kick on aggressively from the front, the race shape flips entirely and hold-up horses gain a winning chance they otherwise lack.

Little Empire and Cancan In The Rain could get into a positional battle immediately behind Eazy On The Eye; if that tussle burns energy in the first two furlongs, both prominent types could find themselves flat in the Ascot straight.
Dannick's going record is almost entirely on Standard surfaces with zero wins on Good turf — watch to see whether the ground inconveniences her before assuming trainer form translates here.

Port Louis's "fades in finish" flag combined with a second race in six days makes her a dangerous in-running layer if she gets to the front or is prominent early — she is likely to drop away sharply once the race intensifies.

Atmosphere's 50-day absence is worth tracking in the betting market — if she drifts pre-race, connections may have doubts about her fitness returning from that layoff, which would significantly alter the hold-up shape probability.

races.name: Charbonnel et Walker EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Ascot Events EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Juddmonte Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qual) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pure Mint
runners_data.note: Won on debut over this exact 6f Ascot Good-ground combination making all under Doyle for the Crisfords — proven pace-setter in the most relevant conditions possible, structurally the most advantaged horse in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Soldier Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher rides this William Knight-trained 2yo who has won over 6f Good and placed over the same, showing a consistent prominent style that should put him right in the slipstream of the leader throughout.

runners_data.name: Does Mary Know
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton has solid recent form (3/30 T14) and this horse ran 2nd in its last over 6f Good, but it is a genuine hold-up type whose closer's profile becomes harder to execute when there is no pace collapse to exploit — the redistribution to midfield reflects a field too light at the rear rather than any change of style.

runners_data.name: Nobelos
runners_data.note: Debut 4th over 6f Good for Charles Hills — raw but bred and placed with a hold-up profile, needing something to go wrong up front to make his run count; Rob Hornby rides and this yard can improve youngsters sharply second time.

runners_data.name: War Chest
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutant for Eve Johnson Houghton with headgear noted (h) and no going profile or form string to assess — a genuine unknown who could fit any part of the field but carries the structural risk of inexperience against horses with relevant form.

runners_data.name: Storm Force Ten
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this Jamie Osborne-trained hold-up type who finished 3rd over 6f Good last time — the step back from 7f to 6f is fine, but the closer profile needs conditions to shift from what the pace map currently suggests.

runners_data.name: Brushstroke
runners_data.note: Ray Dawson partners this TJ Kent-trained 2yo who ran 2nd on debut over 7f at Sandown — dropping back to 6f removes a furlong, and the prominent style should allow him to sit just off Pure Mint and mount a sustained challenge through the final two furlongs.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Mint, the sole confirmed front-runner, will lead from the gates and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Ascot's straight 6f on Good ground — with no rival capable of matching early pace, she will set her own rhythm throughout. Brushstroke and Soldier Of The Sea will press from prominent positions just behind, giving the race a compact but orderly shape rather than a gruelling pace duel. The hold-up horses — Nobelos, Storm Force Ten, and Does Mary Know — will be anchored in the rear third, facing the task of covering ground late against a potentially unchallenged leader. This field holds more hold-up types than can realistically get into a winning position in a race where pace is modest and uncontested; Does Mary Know has been redistributed to midfield but is a genuine closer who is unlikely to find its natural rear position generating sufficient momentum. This shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profile: when one horse controls an uncontested lead on Good ground at Ascot, the rail-hugging pace-setters and chasers have a decisive structural advantage over hold-up horses who must accelerate from further back with no pace collapse to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Mint controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Mint leads without serious early pressure and converts her uncontested lead into a winning performance at the line.
scenarios.body: Pure Mint dictates from gate to line with Brushstroke and Soldier Of The Sea unable to reel her in, as the steady Good-ground tempo suits a horse that has already won over this exact course-distance-going combination.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair mug the leader
scenarios.trigger: If Brushstroke or Soldier Of The Sea tracks Pure Mint closely and outstays her in the final furlong through superior stamina or finishing kick.
scenarios.body: The two prominent racers sit just off the pace and pounce inside the final furlong if Pure Mint ties up or overcooks her early sectionals; both have shown placed form over 6f on Good and understand how to race handily.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves fast enough to string out the field and a closer like Nobelos or Storm Force Ten generates momentum from off the pace to reel in a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: Nobelos ran 4th on debut over this trip on Good but showed raw ability, while Storm Force Ten has placed experience and could pick up the pieces if the front two exhaust each other; this scenario requires the pace to be genuinely taxing, which is against the structural read.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant War Chest surprises
scenarios.trigger: If War Chest, the unexposed and unknown quantity, shows natural ability and a racing style that allows him to feature prominently from the off.
scenarios.body: With no form to assess and unknown going profile, War Chest is a wildcard whose chance is entirely conditional on talent and a natural racing instinct that suits the pace shape; the lightly-raced caveat is real but the probability is low given the structural advantage already held by the known front-end types.

watchPoints.text: Pure Mint's price: if she drifts in the market despite the uncontested lead profile, that signals trainer or jockey intelligence worth noting — conversely, strong support confirms the structural read.

Nobelos and Storm Force Ten will need Pure Mint to visibly tire in the final furlong to land a blow from hold-up positions — watch the sectionals; if the leader is still going strongly passing the 2f pole, the closers are beaten.

War Chest's behaviour in the preliminaries and loading is critical given it is a debutant with headgear already applied — any sign of greenness or reluctance could see it lose ground at the start and render its chance academic.

Soldier Of The Sea and Brushstroke racing too close together could produce interference between the two prominent types if the pace is slow and they converge entering the final 2f — watch for traffic in a compressed mid-group.

Does Mary Know's recent 20-day turnaround and 6th-then-2nd form pattern for Eve Johnson Houghton suggests the yard is finding the horse's best conditions — if it manages to find a prominent position early despite its hold-up profile, treat it as a significant upgrade in danger.

races.name: Big Ascot Food & Wine Festival Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Progressive 6-year-old with an excellent recent 7f record in similar going (1W, 4P from last 5 over this trip); James Doyle is a strong booking and the hold-up style is genuine, though it needs the pace to be honest enough to deliver him late over 7f.

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner returning quickly (9 days) after a mixed spell; a natural racer who wants to bowl along prominently, but with Debrief and multiple others already filling that space, he is likely to be shuffled back slightly from his preferred position and his 0.93 style-fit rating should temper confidence.

runners_data.name: Jolly Roger
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on this Simon & Ed Crisford-trained 4-year-old returning after 137 days off; goes on good and has a solid placing record (0W, 5P in last 5 in similar going), and travelling just off the leader in his natural prominent slot suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Four wins from last six runs is eye-catching and Iain Jardine has the yard in form (3/29 over 14 days); a front-runner at heart who thrives bowling along, he is very likely to find the space ahead already occupied by Debrief, meaning he races a touch behind his comfort zone — style-fit of 0.91 is a real consideration.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: David O'Meara 4-year-old returning quickly (7 days) but the recent form string (033440) shows a horse below his best; Tom Marquand will slot him in the prominent group but he has been running over 6f and stepping back to 7f on good ground is the key question.

runners_data.name: Debrief
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here, Harry Eustace's lightly-raced 3-year-old has won his last two (both over 6f in good going) and now steps up to 7f; the uncontested lead is a significant positional gift, and if the 6f-to-7f stamina extension is within his range, he is ideally placed to exploit the race shape.

runners_data.name: Malachy's Wish
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides the Jamie Osborne-trained 3-year-old, a partnership worth noting; the going form is a concern — only 2 runs on good ground with neither placing (sim-going: 0W, 0P from 2), with best form on Standard, and this trip and surface combination is unproven.

runners_data.name: Suspicious Mindz
runners_data.note: Won last two starts (7f good, 6f good) and has a strong recent profile (2W, 5P from 9 in similar going); Dale Swift takes a prominent berth and the horse's versatility to win over both 6f and 7f suggests the step up in trip and this pace scenario suit.

races.paceDynamic: Debrief is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner 7f Ascot contest and, with no genuine rival to press for the lead, Pierre-Louis Jamin can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a significant positional advantage on good ground. Jolly Roger, Veblen Good, and Suspicious Mindz are the natural prominent types who will compete to sit just behind Debrief, creating a compact early order rather than a pressured pace scenario. The field actually contains more prominent-minded horses than can all settle in their favoured positions: Jonny Concrete and Best Rate are genuine front-of-race types who have been mapped to midfield because the spaces ahead are already taken, meaning both are likely to race slightly out of their natural comfort zone. With a solo leader setting a measured tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind Debrief and quicken off the steady pace — true hold-up horses hunting from the rear face a pace that may not be strong enough to set them up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Debrief Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Debrief dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-strong gallop and the winner comes from the chasing group.
scenarios.body: Debrief goes clear-ish in the straight having conserved energy through a controlled first half, but a prominent tracker with a sharp turn of foot picks him off inside the final furlong; this shape favours horses who can race in the slipstream and quicken on good ground over 7f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debrief Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is soft enough that Debrief, never headed, simply extends clear in the final 2f and holds on.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied, Jamin nurses Debrief through a slow first half then kicks early in the straight, using the advantage of his favourable position to grind out a win before hold-up horses can close; a 3-year-old dropping to 7f on going it handles (4/4) is a genuine threat to go all the way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns out stronger than expected — forcing early leaders wide or setting up a genuine closing run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Aalto and Malachy's Wish, tracking wide from the back, would need the pace to be materially stronger than the projected shape to close enough ground in 7f; Aalto has the best recent 7f form in similar going (3 top-3 finishes from last 5 over 7f) and is the most credible beneficiary if this scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Reshuffled Early Order
scenarios.trigger: If Jonny Concrete or Best Rate, unable to settle out of role, pushes forward and creates a pace injection that scrambles the expected shape.
scenarios.body: A contested lead scrambles Debrief's energy advantage and opens the race up, potentially flattening out front-runners and allowing a fresh hold-up horse to emerge; this is a low-probability scenario given Debrief's tactical flexibility, but Jonny Concrete's strong recent form (4W from last 6) makes the disruption worth noting.

watchPoints.text: Debrief — the sole front-runner with an uncontested lead; if Pierre-Louis Jamin gets a soft lead at a pace of his own choosing over 7f at Ascot on good ground, the tactical advantage is significant and this horse could prove very hard to reel in.

Jonny Concrete and Best Rate — both natural prominent types who cannot get their favoured berth in this race shape; watch for one or both pushing forward early and accidentally injecting pace, which would reshape the whole scenario.

Malachy's Wish — two hold-up horses with 0 placings combined on good ground in the form data; if the pace is as controlled as expected, Saffie Osborne will need a strong late sectional that this race shape may not set up.

Jolly Roger — 137 days off track is a notable absence for a 4-year-old; watch the market closely for any sign of confidence in its readiness, as fitness questions could undermine what is otherwise an ideal positional draw behind the lone front-runner.
Aalto — consistent record at 7f in good going makes this horse a background threat; if it is able to track closer than its hold-up tag suggests, it becomes a bigger factor in Scenarios A and B.

races.name: Ascot Hospitality Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Blue Rc
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four placed efforts from seven on similar Good going, but has a win-less streak and a tricky draw in a compressed prominent group; Rob Hornby keeps faith but a field this busy may squeeze him out of his preferred slot.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has four wins and seven places on Good going from fifteen runs, making him one of the best ground-fit horses in the field; Pat Dobbs is positive on this type and a prominent pitch just behind the leaders suits if the pace stretches the field.

runners_data.name: Hard Endeavor
runners_data.note: Returned from 62 days off which is the longest layoff in the field for an active runner, so fitness is a genuine query; two runs at this trip on Good going have produced a second and fourth, and Rossa Ryan will look to slot prominently and hope the break hasn't blunted his sharpness.

runners_data.name: Urban Lion
runners_data.note: Recorded his one win at this trip on Soft ground and his Good-ground record over a mile reads 9-26-24 showing inconsistency; George Bass takes over in what looks a competitive spot and he may need a stronger pace to reel in the leaders than his form warrants.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who sits patiently and relies on a strong gallop to make ground; James Doyle is a significant booking for Ian Williams and his best run of 3rd on Good over this trip three starts ago shows he retains ability, though he has been out of the frame more often than not of late.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Won two of his last six including back-to-back victories, both on Good ground over a mile, making him one of the best in-form horses here; Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) is an interesting booking for Ed Walker and his hold-up style is precisely what a contested front-running shape will reward.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who wears a hood and uses it to settle in behind the pace; Saffie Osborne rides and his recent record shows a win at this trip on Good and multiple placed runs at the course, though 21 days between runs is a routine gap for this consistent type.

runners_data.name: Spanish Voice
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with three wins on Good ground from six tries including a win at this course and trip; Colin Keane is a strong pilot for Andrew Balding and he will look to control fractions from the front, but Moonfall's presence makes it impossible for Spanish Voice to be uncontested.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose one win in recent form came on Good ground over a mile, but his overall pattern of 6-10-11-19 around that shows unreliability; 20 days since last run is fine but Joe Leavy faces the challenge of finding a clear run from a big field in arrears.

runners_data.name: Moonfall
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner who is unbeaten on Good ground across all seven Good-ground appearances in his career, a striking stat; Jack Callan rides for George Boughey at a track where the straight mile can expose a lack of cover, and his youth makes him a fascinating pace-setter but potentially vulnerable when challenged by the more experienced Spanish Voice.

runners_data.name: Jolly Jack Tar
runners_data.note: 402 days off the track is an enormous layoff and his only previous form at this trip on Good ground produced a single 16th of 16; William Buick's booking is intriguing for John & Thady Gosden and he may strip fitter for the run, but stepping back from ten furlongs after such a break is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: Haggas three-year-old who naturally wants to race prominently but is mapped to midfield because the field is saturated with pace types ahead of him; his best effort was a second on Good ground two starts ago, but his chance is tempered by the likelihood he will find himself racing further back than he wants and unable to influence proceedings from his natural berth.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on Good ground with three thirds from fifteen relevant runs, but genuinely a hold-up type pushed toward midfield on the map because the rear is equally crowded; Kieran O'Neill rides for Margarson and this horse's best chance comes if the pace is truly gruelling, though his OR of 78 is significantly below the top weights.

races.paceDynamic: Spanish Voice and Moonfall are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the break over Ascot's straight mile, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft-pedalled affair. With two horses intent on setting the tempo, the pace is likely to be honest throughout, meaning the race will be run at a consistent rhythm that tests stamina into the final furlong rather than producing a late sprint from a crawl. This contested pace profile favours hold-up horses and patient midfield runners who can travel within themselves before unleashing a sustained late run, particularly those with proven Good-ground finishing ability. The field contains more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Blue Rc, Classic, Hard Endeavor, Urban Lion, and the redistributed Zennor Storm all carry prominent tendencies, and with Spanish Voice and Moonfall already committed to the front, it is Spanish Voice and Moonfall who will secure the rail and lead, leaving several prominent types fighting for position just behind, compressing the midfield and benefiting the genuine hold-up performers who are content to sit and wait.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Spanish Voice and Moonfall push each other along at a genuine clip and the prominent group crowds behind them, leaving hold-up horses to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The sustained honest gallop burns out the front two entering the final two furlongs, opening the door for hold-up horses sweeping off the pace with a clear run; Good ground at Ascot rewards a staying gallop-type finish rather than a sharp turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Spanish Voice or Moonfall gains a clear advantage early and the other drops away, allowing a sole front-runner to control the tempo.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner who controls fractions on Good ground at Ascot's mile can dictate a manageable pace before quickening clear in the straight, and Spanish Voice's three wins from six Good-ground runs makes her the more likely candidate to dominate if Moonfall is outgunned.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Race, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk but not extreme and the prominent bunch just behind the leaders can sustain their momentum through the straight without being caught too wide or pocketed.
scenarios.body: Horses settled in second or third early ground can benefit if the front two tie each other up without fully combusting, leaving prominent types with enough petrol to strike; Classic and Hard Endeavor both have strong Good-ground profiles at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Burst, Held Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more contested than it looks and the field strings out, creating a truly attritional gallop where only the deepest stayer or sharpest late finisher can deliver.
scenarios.body: A genuinely gruelling early pace would theoretically hand the race to the furthest back, but given that the redistributed hold-up types such as Mythical Guest and Zennor Storm are not fully operating in their natural roles, the probability of this scenario delivering is discounted accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Spanish Voice and Moonfall will fight for the lead from the off — watch whether either horse capitulates before halfway, because if one subsides early the other controls fractions and the race shape shifts entirely toward SCENARIO_B.

Jolly Jack Tar has been off 402 days and drops back to a mile for the first time in his last five starts — William Buick's positive ride could produce a career-best fresh effort or the horse could be dangerously underdone; monitor in the market.

The prominent group of Blue Rc, Classic, Hard Endeavor, and Urban Lion will all be competing for the same small strip of ground in the first two furlongs behind the front two — watch for crowding, interference, or any of them being shuffled further back than intended.

Arctic Thunder's back-to-back wins on Good ground over this exact trip make him the form horse for the likely race shape — watch whether Ashley Lewis settles him cleanly in rear, because a clear run from off the pace in this scenario is his primary weapon.

Moonfall's seven-from-seven record on Good ground is the most striking going stat in the race — watch if the market shortens him significantly before post time, as backers of this data point could make him a shorter price than his three-year-old allowance and inexperience at the top level might justify.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: First Legion
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Richard Hannon who drops to 87 OR following a run of placed efforts at 6f on Good; steps up to 7f here which is worth monitoring given all five recent runs are at six, though the Good turf suits and Shane Foley provides experience.|

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in electric current form — two wins from three 7f starts on Good going, trained by Herrington who fires at 1/11 over 14 days, and Lewis Edmunds a strong booking; the trip and surface are exactly what he wants.|

runners_data.name: Luansobe
runners_data.note: Prominent-going 3yo for Charlie Fellowes who won over this exact 7f trip on Good and has a placed effort in the same conditions; has been off 55 days and a wide draw or traffic issue could complicate matters, but course-distance form is solid.|

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner stepping back from 8f to 7f for David Marnane, who saddles a winner in 14 days; two wins over a mile on Good make the trip drop interesting, and his willingness to fight from the front is the key tactical variable in this race.|

runners_data.name: Star Of Commala
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead-seeker with back-to-back wins on Standard going, stepping onto Good turf for the first time — the going switch is the primary concern; ridden by 7lb claimer Molly Keegan-Price which adds risk if a tactical fight develops early with Hambelton.|

runners_data.name: Golden Brown
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type who has shown consistent placed form at 6f on Good for Ed Walker, who is in strong recent strike-rate form at 7/43 over 14 days; stepping up to 7f for the first time is the one query, though Tom Marquand is an excellent judge of pace.|

runners_data.name: Sapphire Steps
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Richard Hannon (cold 14-day figures at 0/42) who has struggled to land a blow in recent starts, going 0W1P from eight runs on Good and showing no form at 8f; the trip is familiar but the finishing kick has been absent.|

runners_data.name: King Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse ridden by James Doyle, returning from a 120-day absence for Hugo Palmer; won over 7f on Soft and has course form over the trip, but the layoff is significant and the drop from Soft to Good may slightly blunt his finishing effort.|

runners_data.name: You Sexy Thing
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner by nature for Richard Spencer — in good recent form (3/14 trainer strike over 14 days) — who is mapped forward to midfield because the field's abundance of hold-up types prevents all of them settling at the rear; its chance is somewhat tempered by the likelihood it races ahead of its preferred position.|

races.paceDynamic: Star Of Commala and Hambelton are both confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner 7f handicap at Ascot, setting up a genuinely contested early pace from the gates that should produce an honest, pressure-filled gallop throughout. Star Of Commala, ridden by a 7lb claimer in Molly Keegan-Price, arrives on the back of back-to-back wins on Standard going and may lack the tactical flexibility to settle if Hambelton, a proven front-runner who steps back from 8f, immediately challenges for supremacy. The resulting friction at the head of affairs on Good turf over 7f is likely to play into the hands of prominent-to-midfield types who can sit just off the speed and pounce when the leaders begin to tire in the final two furlongs — a race shape that suits organised, settled horses over straight-line territory. The field carries more hold-up and prominent runners than the map can accommodate at the rear; Star Of Commala and Hambelton are most likely to actually secure the lead, with You Sexy Thing — a genuine hold-up type — pushed forward to midfield and unlikely to race from its natural berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Chasers
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Commala and Hambelton fight for the front and set a true honest gallop, burning themselves out by the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The pace duel creates a genuinely run race where horses who track the speed in third to fifth position receive a strong energy-conservation advantage and can mow down the tiring leaders inside the final furlong. Raging Raj, prominent-going and in red-hot form with two recent wins at 7f on Good, and Golden Brown, a consistent prominent racer suited by this trip, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hambelton Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Commala is unable to match Hambelton's early pace and drops off the lead, allowing Hambelton to control the race on its own terms at a measured gallop.
scenarios.body: A controlled solo lead with Hambelton dictating fractions suits its recent winning profile at distances where it has impressed stepping up from 6f, and a metronomic gallop gives it the best possible chance of lasting home under Luke McAteer. Prominent-tracking horses like Raging Raj would still be dangerous if the gallop is not strong enough to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field bunches through the middle stages, allowing horses settled in midfield to produce a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: King Of Thunder, held up by James Doyle, and First Legion, stepping back from short-priced form over 6-7f, would benefit from a race that sets up for a late, sweeping finish rather than an attritional grind. Both have the turn of foot from off the pace to make this viable if the tempo is genuinely honest without being frenetic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Outbattle Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pair of front-runners settle into an unexpectedly comfortable rhythm and the hold-up and midfield horses fail to quicken sufficiently to close the gap.
scenarios.body: In this shape the tactical dispute between Star Of Commala and Hambelton resolves early with one dominant, the field fails to muster a coordinated challenge, and the race is run out in front. This is a low-probability outcome given the weight of prominent and hold-up types capable of closing, and relies on the pace duo conserving more energy than the scenario predicts.

watchPoints.text: Star Of Commala vs Hambelton — watch the first two furlongs closely; if both are hard ridden from the gates, the pace duel could set an extremely fierce early tempo that compromises both their finishing efforts.|

King Of Thunder returns from 120 days off — if James Doyle drops him out last as expected, the 7f trip at Ascot may not be long enough for a horse that needs a truly searching gallop after a lengthy absence to find full fitness.|

Golden Brown steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time in a race where the pace is likely honest — if the extra furlong is within his stamina range, Tom Marquand can exploit his prominent position, but it is an untested query worth tracking.|

You Sexy Thing is a hold-up horse likely to find itself racing in midfield rather than at the back — Saffie Osborne will need to judge whether to push forward or get outpaced early, and the style displacement could cost the horse its ideal rhythm.|

Raging Raj's trainer Herrington runs at 1/11 strike rate in the past 14 days — small sample but the horse's own recent form at the trip and going is the stronger evidence; watch whether Lewis Edmunds positions him to track the pace duel from second or third.|
